title: MeanResidue: a Lean 4 formalization of mean quadratic residues, floor sums of square roots, and the conjectures of Chamberland and Dilcher
description: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the proof of the conjectures of M. Chamberland and K. Dilcher (arXiv:2510.04387, Section 7). The conjectures have probably been proved before: Conjecture 7.2 in an AI-generated write-up on the Principia Math platform (MathDB problem 370786, September 2026), and, according to its listing, all five in a preprint by S. K. Jha posted on ResearchGate (October 2026), which the author has not been able to consult. No priority is claimed for the conjectures; what this software offers is a machine-checked proof, with the statements checked by Lean's comparator and the proofs replayed in the Lean, nanoda and con-ron kernels. Version 1.0.2 is listed in the Palomar registry (entry PALOMAR-2026-11-24-000022); version 1.0.3 changes only the documentation. For every n >= 1, the floor sum f(n) = sum_{j <= n/4} floor(sqrt(jn)) - (n^2-1)/12 is expressed through the mean quadratic residue S_n and the number s(n) of square roots of 0 modulo n, and (n - s(n))/2 - S_n = sum_{d | n} G(d), where G(d) is a sawtooth sum of the Moebius-inverted root counts. G vanishes on d = 1, 2 (mod 4), equals the Bernoulli form -(1/c) sum_{a<c} a (-c/a) of the class number at fundamental discriminants -c, and satisfies the conductor recursion G(l^2 c) = (l - (-c/l)) G(c) for every prime l and every c > 0 with c = 0, 3 (mod 4); with Dirichlet's class number formula and the conductor formula (quoted, not formalized) this is G(c) = h*(-c). Consequences: Conjectures 7.1 (with a sign corrected), 7.2, 7.3 and 7.4 of Chamberland and Dilcher, their formulas (7.3), (7.4), Bunyakovsky's identity and Proposition 1.2, in Bernoulli form, and Conjecture 7.5 (the limits of f(n)/n), unconditionally, from the bound defect(n)^2 <= n sqrt(n) (1 + log n)^3 proved by Fourier analysis on Z/n and Weyl differencing (also, as in the note, from a class number bound stated as a hypothesis). Also: square roots modulo prime powers, including 2. The formula for S_n is the case a = 1 of Proposition A.2 of Skoruppa and Zagier (Invent. Math. 94, 1988). No sorry, no native_decide; standard axioms only. The folder numerics holds the Python scripts for the numerical checks of the accompanying note (exact rational arithmetic, class numbers counted from reduced forms), with their outputs; they are independent of the formalization.
notes: AI assistance: the Lean code in this record was drafted and repaired by Claude (Anthropic), an AI model, from the statements and proofs of the companion note "Mean quadratic residues, floor sums of square roots, and class numbers: the conjectures of Chamberland and Dilcher" (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24508994), and compiled locally with lake; the Python scripts in the folder numerics were also written by Claude. Every proof is checked by the Lean kernel, and Lean's comparator checks the statements against the proofs, which are replayed in the Lean, nanoda and con-ron kernels. The author, Joseph S. Farland, chose the scope, directed the work, and is responsible for the contents. No external human reviewer has checked the formalization.
